SMTO-GML-0014 — This email is too long to forward with its text included

GUID: 20d42101-7bfd-43b8-8ab0-6f95040f1dd1
Slug: gmail-forward-body-too-large
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The email you wanted to forward is too long for SMTO to copy into a new message without cutting part of it off. SMTO stopped instead of sending an incomplete copy. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to forward the email "as an attachment". Forwarding as an attachment sends the complete original email as a file, so nothing is cut off.
  2. If you only need part of the email, ask SMTO to forward it without the original text and to write a short summary or quote the part you need. A shorter message fits easily, and you choose what is left out instead of it being cut off silently.
  3. Before you approve sending, check the recipients and the message SMTO shows you. This makes sure the forward goes to the right people with the content you expect.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the forward as sent, and the email appears in your Gmail Sent folder.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to just cut the email shorter without telling the recipients that part is missing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail forward preparation found the original message body truncated at 1,000,000 characters while include_original was requested, so it refused to build an incomplete inline forward.

What this means

  • Forward preparation detects truncated source-body extraction while include_original is requested. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Forward preparation detects truncated source-body extraction while include_original is requested.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect source extraction completeness and whether including the original was explicitly requested.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._mime (kind=forward) extracts the original body with a 1,000,000-character limit and raises gmail_forward_body_too_large when it is truncated and include_original is true. Use as_attachment=true to forward the full original as message/rfc822 (.eml), or set include_original=false and summarize or reference the original content.
  • Reduce or split the forwarded content without silently truncating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Complete intended source content is available or a deliberate supported forwarding choice avoids silent loss.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
